mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 280.0 indicates persistent inflation, triggering central bank tightening that increases equity discount rates and causes negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 280.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate earnings expectations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A tight labor market (UNRATE below 4.0%) fuels wage growth and consumer spending, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 100.0 signals economic contraction, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate below 3.5% indicates extreme labor market tightness, increasing wage pressures and inflation expectations that prompt central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS above 4.0%), higher interest rates reduce equity valuations by increasing discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing starts (HOUST above 1700.0) indicate robust consumer spending and economic growth, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1700.0.
